Regence BlueShield  
Customer Service / Appeals Department

Re: Appeal of prior authorization denial  
Member: Jordan Brooks  
Member ID: W436997835  
Reference number: POC-41FE448BEA-64337  
Requested service: Hip arthroscopy  
CPT: 29914  
Plan: Regence BlueShield Commercial/ACA, Washington

Dear Regence Appeals Department:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29914, hip arthroscopy with femoroplasty. The denial identifies medical necessity as the reason for the adverse determination. Based on my documented symptoms, diagnostic findings, failed conservative treatment, and functional limitations, this procedure is medically necessary and should be authorized.

I have experienced nine months of progressive hip pain that has not improved with rest. The pain is sharp and located in the anterior groin, particularly with sitting and pivoting. I cannot run or squat. Examination documented positive provocative testing on the affected side, and my range of motion is limited by pain.

The diagnostic findings identify a structural condition that corresponds to the requested procedure. A June 13, 2026 MRI arthrogram demonstrated an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement and an alpha angle of 68 degrees. The joint space remains preserved, with Tönnis grade 0. These findings support treatment directed at the cam lesion rather than treatment of advanced degenerative arthritis.

I have also completed substantial conservative treatment without adequate relief:

- Supervised physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization, together with activity modification, for 14 weeks from April 9, 2026 through July 16, 2026.
- Twenty documented physical therapy visits, with the discharge note recording the completed course.
- NSAID treatment for eight months, with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on April 21, 2026, which provided only two weeks of partial relief.

The condition continues to cause substantial pain and restricts basic and higher-level activities despite these measures. The requested arthroscopic treatment is directed at the documented cam-type impingement and associated labral tear. My surgeon, Marchetti, MD, orthopedic surgery, submitted the prior authorization request.

There are no documented contraindications identified in the clinical summary. I have no active infection or untreated substance-use condition, am a non-smoker, and have a BMI of 29.

The specific Regence commercial/ACA medical policy, clinical review criteria, policy number, version, and effective date applied to this denial were not identified in the notice or made available in the public materials reviewed for this appeal. Accordingly, the plan’s medical-necessity language has not been quoted here. Please provide the exact criteria applied to CPT 29914, the policy version and effective date, the clinical rationale for the denial, and the records relied upon in making the determination.

Please conduct a new review by a clinician who was not involved in the initial decision and overturn the denial. If Regence maintains the denial, please provide a detailed explanation identifying each criterion that was not satisfied and specify what additional clinical information is required.

Please treat this as a timely Level One internal appeal. The denial notice states that the appeal must be received by February 19, 2027. Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide the appeal determination in writing.

Enclosures:

- Denial notice
- MRI arthrogram report dated June 13, 2026
- Physical therapy discharge note documenting treatment from April 9, 2026 through July 16, 2026 and 20 completed visits
- Medication and treatment history
- Corticosteroid injection record dated April 21, 2026
- Orthopedic examination and clinical notes
- Prior authorization request from Marchetti, MD
- Any additional supporting medical records

Sincerely,

Jordan Brooks
